threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still look up at the trains when they rumble overhead, while the rest of us just carry on chatting like it’s a Sunday stroll.
Caught a glimpse of a lad on the N133 rapping to himself, but when he noticed me staring, he just smiled and went back to mumbling. Classic Brixton vibe.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The day I heard a group of kids arguing over which Kebab shop was the best – their passion made me realize I was officially part of the Neukölln family.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg can you find a late-night kebab shop where the owner plays deep house and hands you your döner like it's a work of art.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: Only a true local knows to check the BART delay app before heading to Dolores Park on a sunny Saturday. Otherwise, it’s a gamble on those crowded trains.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Watched a guy on the 31 refuse to let the driver close the doors because he was trying to pick up a dropped sandwich. Classic Tenderloin hustle.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists often miss the fact that the locals never use the word 'Gaudí' outside of the context of a building. It’s just part of life here.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell they're new by the way they still try to use Google Maps to navigate the narrow streets instead of just going with the flow.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still avoid the healed cobblestones thinking they’re a hazard, but the locals are dodging buses with a smile.
Caught a guy on the 59 last night rapping about lost love; sounded like he could've been on stage at the Academy. Whole bus just vibed with him.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The day I saw an impromptu dance party break out on a Tuesday afternoon at the neck of Weserstraße. Just another Neukölln moment.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: You can catch a spontaneous street art tour while waiting for the U-Bahn; the walls here are alive with fresh layers every week.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can tell the locals by the way they roll their eyes at tourists wandering into Dolores Park with styrofoam takeout instead of a picnic basket.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy on the 14 Mission juggling oranges for tips while the bus got stuck in traffic. Muni's chaos somehow makes for the best street performances.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists often think Gràcia is all about the squares, but it’s the hidden street art and local bars that really tell the neighborhood’s story.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a recent arrival by their bewilderment at the metro's pay-per-zone system—locals just swipe and go, no hesitation.
